body_markdown:
Atoms has gained attention in the AI app builder space with its multi-agent approach to product development, coordinating specialized AI agents for engineering, product management, SEO, and advertising. According to the 2026 Stack Overflow survey,[65.9% of 17,464 respondents](https://survey.stackoverflow.co/2026/ai/data/ai-select) reported using AI coding assistants or coding agents at work. However, teams exploring AI-powered app development have different priorities: some need mobile app deployment, others want to build in their existing AI assistants, and many want to understand how credits and hosting affect ongoing costs.


This guide examines eight Atoms alternatives for non-technical founders, freelancers, and development teams. For readers already using Claude or ChatGPT,[Floot](https://floot.com/) offers a full-stack platform with an MCP connector, managed infrastructure, and no separate Floot AI build-credit charge for connector-based development.


Pricing and product details were checked on November 23, 2026, for readers planning projects in 2027. Prices are in USD and shown with monthly billing unless stated otherwise.


## **Key Takeaways**


- **Build from familiar AI assistants** : Floot's[MCP connector](https://floot.com/docs/integrations/build-from-claude-and-chatgpt) supports Claude, Codex, Cursor, and compatible ChatGPT configurations. Available development actions depend on the client's connector permissions.
- **Mobile publishing broadens options** : Floot offers[iOS and Android builds](https://floot.com/docs/mobile-apps/creating-mobile-apps-in-floot) without requiring a local Mac or Xcode installation. Developer accounts and app-store approval are still required.
- **Full-stack infrastructure matters** : Floot combines[managed PostgreSQL](https://floot.com/blog/ai-app-builders-built-in-databases) , authentication, hosting, file storage, and backend services for apps that need saved data.
- **Building and hosting costs differ** : Floot is[free to start](https://floot.com/en/pricing) and measures connector operations in building actions, with separate hosting allowances and AI credits for optional features.
- **Ownership is distinct from export** : Floot users own their code and data on every plan, while[complete code downloads](https://floot.com/docs/faqs/code-data-and-exports) require a paid plan.


## **Understanding AI App Builders in 2027**


AI app builders have evolved beyond simple code generation tools into platforms that support full-stack development. Before choosing one, evaluate the services needed for a working application:


- **Database integration** : Managed data storage and suitable backup or recovery options.
- **User authentication** : Sign-up, login, and supported social sign-in methods.
- **Backend runtime** : Server-side APIs, business logic, and scheduled tasks where required.
- **Hosting and deployment** : Managed infrastructure, domain options, and clear usage limits.
- **Code ownership** : Ownership and export terms, including plan restrictions and potential migration work.


Atoms emphasizes a multi-agent workflow where specialized PM, Engineer, SEO, and Ads agents coordinate different stages of product development. That approach may suit users who want building and growth activities in one environment. Other users prioritize working through an existing AI assistant, controlling infrastructure requirements, or packaging apps for mobile stores.


## **1. Floot**


[Floot](https://floot.com/) is a full-stack app-building platform with an MCP connector that lets users create, edit, and publish applications through supported AI assistants, including Claude, Codex, Cursor, and compatible ChatGPT configurations. The connected AI assistant handles development tasks while Floot supplies managed infrastructure. The actions available in a given workflow depend on the client's connector permissions and enabled tools.


### **Key Capabilities for App Building**


Floot is designed for non-technical founders and operators who want working web and mobile applications with saved data, user accounts, and hosting, rather than only generated interfaces. Its[connector workflow](https://floot.com/docs/integrations/build-from-claude-and-chatgpt) connects a capable AI assistant to services Floot manages.


- **MCP connector integration** : Create, inspect, edit, test, and publish projects from supported AI clients, subject to their tool permissions.
- **Full-stack infrastructure** : Managed PostgreSQL, serverless backend endpoints, file storage, and CDN-backed delivery. See the[database guide](https://floot.com/blog/ai-app-builders-built-in-databases) .
- **Built-in authentication** : Email/password sign-in and brokered Google and Microsoft OAuth. Read about[user authentication](https://floot.com/blog/ai-app-builders-built-in-user-authentication) .
- **Payments and email** : Transactional email and[Stripe payments](https://floot.com/docs/integrations/payments) , with a paid Floot plan needed to accept live payments through Floot's built-in Stripe connection.
- **Mobile app packaging** : Build[iOS and Android apps](https://floot.com/docs/mobile-apps/creating-mobile-apps-in-floot) from a Floot web project using managed cloud builds.
- **SEO controls** : Pre-rendering, configurable metadata, and sitemaps for published web applications through[SEO tools](https://floot.com/en/seo) .


### **Use Cases**


Floot serves non-technical founders building MVPs, freelancers creating client projects, and teams creating internal tools. Suitable applications include appointment booking systems, customer portals, real estate workflows, online shops, and business dashboards. Users with eligible Claude or ChatGPT access can build with their existing assistant rather than buying a second set of Floot AI build credits. Floot complements Codex and Cursor rather than replacing those development tools.


### **Pricing Structure**


The[live pricing page](https://floot.com/en/pricing) lists three Floot plans:


- **Free ($0/month)** : 100 building actions/day, 3,000 one-time starter AI credits, a one-time $3 hosting credit, and 2 mobile app builds/month.
- **Pro ($25/month)** : 1,000 building actions/day, 5,000 AI credits/month, $10/month in included hosting usage, 12 mobile builds/month, and custom domains.
- **Power ($100/month)** : 5,000 building actions/day, 15,000 AI credits/month, $25/month in included hosting usage, and unlimited mobile builds.


Yearly billing offers two months free. Building through a supported connector uses the connected assistant's subscription or usage entitlement and Floot building actions; it does not incur a separate Floot AI build-credit charge. Image generation is an exception and can use Floot credits. Hosting beyond allowances draws on prepaid credit, and optional auto-reload is off by default. Users own their code and data on all plans, but[project ZIP export](https://floot.com/docs/faqs/code-data-and-exports) requires a paid plan.


### **Use With Mobile App Stores**


The[mobile publishing guide](https://floot.com/docs/mobile-apps/creating-mobile-apps-in-floot) explains how Floot builds apps without requiring a local Mac, Xcode, or Android Studio setup. Apple TestFlight connections are available on every Floot plan, while connecting Google Play requires a paid plan. Users must have the applicable Apple and Google developer accounts, and final store review and approval are not guaranteed.


## **2. Lovable**


Lovable is an AI app builder with a visual editor and managed cloud-backed infrastructure. It supports prompt-based development, interface refinement, and full-stack web applications. For a direct perspective on overlapping workflows, see Floot's[Lovable comparison](https://floot.com/blog/floot-vs-lovable-compare-ai-no-code-platforms-2025) .


### **Key Capabilities**


- **Visual editor** : Design tools and direct interface manipulation.
- **Backend infrastructure** : Lovable Cloud provides managed PostgreSQL, authentication, and storage, with an option to connect a separate Supabase project.
- **Code synchronization** : Two-way Git integration with GitHub, GitLab, and Bitbucket.
- **Template library** : Starting points for common application types.
- **Team collaboration** : Shared workspaces and role-based controls, with additional business-plan options.


### **Use Cases**


Lovable fits teams prioritizing visual design and web application interfaces. It supports websites, prototypes, internal tools, and MVPs that benefit from repeated design refinement.


### **Pricing Structure**


- **Free ($0/month)** : 5 daily build credits, capped at 30/month, plus 20 monthly Cloud credits.
- **Pro ($25/month)** : 100 monthly credits, custom domains, and additional workspace controls.
- **Business ($50/month)** : 100 monthly credits, with advanced workspace, security, and access features.


### **Organizational Fit**


Lovable suits users who prefer its visual design environment and web-focused workflow. It also provides MCP connectivity. Floot uses its connected assistant's development capabilities and measures connector operations through building actions instead of charging a second Floot AI build-credit balance. See more[Lovable alternatives](https://floot.com/blog/best-lovable-alternatives-in-2026-apps-that-can-actually-ship) .


## **3. Bolt.new**


Bolt.new provides browser-based AI app development with an integrated coding environment. Bolt Cloud supplies managed database, hosting, and authentication services. Floot's[Bolt comparison](https://floot.com/blog/floot-vs-bolt-which-ai-app-builder-is-better-in-2026) explores their different building workflows.


### **Key Capabilities**


- **Browser IDE** : Code editing and immediate preview in the browser.
- **Framework flexibility** : Support for several JavaScript frameworks, including React, Vue, Svelte, and Astro.
- **Bolt Cloud** : Integrated database, hosting, and authentication services.
- **Code access** : Direct editing and export options.
- **Fast iteration** : Preview changes while developing.


### **Use Cases**


Bolt.new suits users who want AI-assisted web development in a browser IDE. It supports rapid prototyping and full-stack JavaScript application workflows, including hands-on code changes.


### **Pricing Structure**


- **Free ($0/month)** : Up to 300,000 tokens/day and 1 million tokens/month.
- **Pro ($25/month)** : Starts at 10 million tokens/month, with hosting and custom domains.
- **Teams ($30/member/month)** : Per-member subscription with centralized billing and team administration.


### **Organizational Fit**


Bolt.new offers direct access to the code and a browser-based development workspace. Teams preferring to work through supported existing AI assistants can compare that workflow with Floot's connector model.


## **4. Replit**


Replit provides a cloud coding workspace with AI assistance, support for numerous programming languages, and collaborative development. Floot's[Replit comparison](https://floot.com/blog/floot-vs-replit-compare-ai-vibecoding-platforms-in-2026) explains the differences between an integrated coding workspace and managed app infrastructure.


### **Key Capabilities**


- **Multi-language support** : Python, JavaScript, Go, Ruby, and other programming languages.
- **AI Agent** : AI-assisted building and code changes within the workspace.
- **Collaborative coding** : Shared development environments and collaboration controls.
- **Deployment** : Built-in hosting and support for custom domains.
- **Developer tools** : A code editor, terminal, and runtime controls.


### **Use Cases**


Replit suits developers and learners who need a flexible coding environment rather than only a guided app builder. It can support web apps, scripts, backend services, and other programming projects.


### **Pricing Structure**


- **Starter/Free ($0/month)** : A limited entry-level workspace and AI usage.
- **Core ($20/month)** : Expanded AI usage, development features, and $20 in monthly usage credits for supported models.
- **Pro ($100/month)** : Higher monthly usage allowances, more parallel agents, and additional collaboration features.


### **Organizational Fit**


Replit works well for users who want conventional coding tools alongside AI assistance. Non-technical teams primarily interested in publishing apps with managed PostgreSQL, authentication, and hosting may prefer a narrower full-stack app workflow.


## **5. Base44**


Base44 offers a prompt-to-app workflow. Wix acquired the company in June 2025, and Base44 continues to operate as a standalone AI app-building platform. For the differences in building models, see Floot's[Base44 comparison](https://floot.com/blog/floot-vs-base44-which-ai-app-builder-is-better-in-2026) .


### **Key Capabilities**


- **Prompt-to-app** : Generate applications from natural-language requirements.
- **Managed backend** : Built-in database, authentication, and hosting services.
- **Quick prototyping** : Create and refine business tools and MVPs.
- **Visual editing** : Modify interfaces after generation.


### **Use Cases**


Base44 suits users building database-backed tools such as portals, dashboards, and internal workflows through a single prompt-driven interface.


### **Pricing Structure**


- **Free ($0/month)** : 25 message credits and 100 integration credits/month.
- **Starter ($20/month)** : 100 message credits and 2,000 integration credits/month.
- **Builder ($50/month)** : 250 message credits and 10,000 integration credits/month, with GitHub integration.
- **Pro ($100/month)** : 500 message credits and 20,000 integration credits/month.


### **Organizational Fit**


Base44 fits users who prefer a standalone conversational builder with integrated backend services. Teams comparing development costs should distinguish its message and integration credits from Floot's building actions and separate hosting usage.


## **6. v0 by Vercel**


v0 is an AI-powered development tool for creating interfaces and full-stack applications with integrations for backend logic and data services.


### **Key Capabilities**


- **UI generation** : AI-assisted creation of React components and interfaces.
- **Vercel integration** : Deployment to Vercel hosting.
- **Component iteration** : Refinement of generated UI through conversation.
- **Design focus** : Visual interface generation and editing.


### **Use Cases**


v0 serves frontend developers, designers, and product teams creating reusable UI components or full-stack web applications through the Vercel ecosystem.


### **Pricing Structure**


- **Free ($0/month)** : Limited daily messages, visual editing, and deployment capabilities.
- **Plus ($30/user/month)** : $30 in included monthly credits per user and team collaboration features.
- **Business ($100/user/month)** : $30 in included monthly credits per user with additional privacy and organizational controls.


### **Organizational Fit**


v0 fits teams using Vercel and React-based development workflows. Teams planning a database-backed application should also evaluate their authentication, data integrations, and hosting configuration.


## **7. Bubble**


Bubble is a visual app-building platform with workflow automation, integrated data storage, plugins, and native mobile development options.


### **Key Capabilities**


- **Visual development** : Drag-and-drop interface building with workflow logic.
- **Plugin marketplace** : Third-party integrations and extensions.
- **Built-in database** : Native data storage and management.
- **Workflow automation** : Visual business logic and process design.
- **Mobile app development** : Native iOS and Android building through Bubble's visual platform.


### **Use Cases**


Bubble suits teams building marketplaces, customer-facing business applications, and workflow-heavy tools without writing traditional application code.


### **Pricing Structure**


The prices below are for **web-only plans, billed monthly** . Bubble sells separate Mobile and Web & Mobile plans.


- **Free ($0/month)** : Build and test web and mobile apps; live publishing requires a paid plan.
- **Starter ($39/month)** : Live web publishing and custom domains.
- **Growth ($134/month)** : Increased usage allowances and advanced web capabilities.
- **Team ($399/month)** : More collaboration and administration features.


### **Organizational Fit**


Bubble fits users who prefer visual programming over conversational building. It also offers native mobile development, although mobile publishing requires a suitable Mobile or Web & Mobile plan and separate developer accounts.


## **8. ChatGPT Sites**


ChatGPT Sites lets eligible users create, preview, publish, and share interactive websites and lightweight applications from ChatGPT without configuring a separate web development environment.


### **Key Capabilities**


- **Chat-based creation** : Build and refine sites through conversational prompts.
- **Managed hosting** : Publish and share sites privately or publicly, subject to permissions.
- **Persistent data** : Store supported application records and files within usage limits.
- **Connected apps** : Create tools that use visitors' connected services under their existing permissions.


### **Use Cases**


ChatGPT Sites suits dashboards, trackers, resource hubs, forms, and other lightweight applications. Teams needing Floot's managed PostgreSQL environment, customized login workflows, or iOS and Android packaging should compare those needs separately.


### **Pricing Structure**


- **Eligible paid ChatGPT plans** : Sites is available with Plus, Pro, Business, and Enterprise subscriptions, subject to workspace settings. There is no separate Sites subscription tier.
- **Building and editing** : Counts toward the subscriber's Codex usage entitlement.
- **Hosting and storage** : Subject to Sites usage and storage limits. Hosting is currently included for Plus and Pro; enterprise hosting charges are currently waived.


### **Organizational Fit**


ChatGPT Sites suits users who want a hosted site-building experience entirely inside ChatGPT. Floot instead provides a separate managed full-stack infrastructure layer that a compatible ChatGPT configuration can operate through an MCP connector. ChatGPT Sites is not available on Free or Go plans.


## **Why Floot Is a Strong Atoms Alternative**


Floot helps non-technical founders and business operators build apps that need persistent data, logins, and a working backend. Through its[MCP connector](https://floot.com/docs/integrations/build-from-claude-and-chatgpt) , supported AI assistants handle permitted development tasks while Floot manages the infrastructure. That keeps the app-building process within familiar tools without requiring users to configure every service themselves.


- **Existing assistants** : Build through Claude, Codex, Cursor, or compatible ChatGPT configurations, subject to permissions.
- **Saved data and logins** : Use[PostgreSQL and authentication](https://floot.com/blog/ai-app-builders-built-in-user-authentication) for customer and internal applications.
- **Web and mobile delivery** : Publish web apps and create[mobile builds](https://floot.com/docs/mobile-apps/creating-mobile-apps-in-floot) .
- **Transparent allowances** : Review[Floot pricing](https://floot.com/en/pricing) for building actions, hosting, and optional AI credits.


Floot is[free to start](https://floot.com/en/pricing) . Paid plans raise the action and hosting allowances, while code ownership remains with the user and full project downloads are available on paid plans.


## **Frequently Asked Questions**


### **What is the difference between Floot and Atoms?**


Floot provides a[full-stack MCP connector](https://floot.com/docs/integrations/build-from-claude-and-chatgpt) and managed infrastructure for apps built through supported AI assistants. Atoms coordinates a standalone team of specialized agents for development and growth tasks. Floot's available actions depend on the connected AI client's permissions.


### **Can Floot deploy iOS and Android apps?**


Yes. Floot's[mobile building workflow](https://floot.com/docs/mobile-apps/creating-mobile-apps-in-floot) packages projects into installable iOS and Android apps. Free includes two builds per month, Pro includes twelve, and Power includes unlimited builds. Apple developer-account connections are available on every Floot plan; Google Play connections require a paid plan. Store approval remains separate.


### **How do Floot building actions differ from AI credits?**


Floot's[pricing structure](https://floot.com/en/pricing) measures connector reads, edits, and tests through building actions. Free, Pro, and Power list daily allowances of 100, 1,000, and 5,000. Connected assistant subscriptions or their usage entitlements supply the AI model. Floot AI credits apply to optional AI features and image generation, while hosting usage is billed separately beyond allowances.


### **Does Floot include a database and user authentication?**


Yes. Floot provides[managed PostgreSQL](https://floot.com/blog/ai-app-builders-built-in-databases) , email/password sign-in, brokered Google and Microsoft OAuth, file storage, and hosting. These services support applications with customer accounts and saved information. Developers should still configure application-specific permissions and test their workflows before release.


### **Who owns the code built with Floot?**


Floot users retain ownership of their code, data, and intellectual property on every plan. Database export is available on all plans, while downloading the full project as a runnable ZIP requires a paid plan. The[export guide](https://floot.com/docs/faqs/code-data-and-exports) explains the process. Self-hosting exported code may require replacing Floot-managed services.
